records.text: Candace Owens said the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office confirmed that only deputies witnessed Desmond Holly shoot himself.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Now when the officers and Desmond Holly had both moved out of frame, out of the view of the roofer's camera, a final shot rings out, not captured by the camera, it was Desmond shooting himself. ... The sheriff's office has since confirmed that only the deputies were the witnesses to Holly shooting himself after they gave their commands.

verification.notes: JCSO records confirm that deputies confronted Holly at gunpoint and that he then suffered a self-inflicted wound. Later records report that he shouted about dropping the weapon before shooting himself. The reviewed official update does not expressly establish that deputies were the only witnesses, so that exclusivity remains unconfirmed.

records.text: Candace Owens said the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office acknowledged in its October 10 update that mutual-aid officers asked locked-down teachers and students to open doors, while county deputies followed protocol.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: The Jefferson County Sheriff's Office actually acknowledged this in their October 10th update and said. That Jefferson County's deputies followed the protocol correctly and it was the outside or mutual aid officers from neighboring agencies who started going door to door asking people to open up and the sheriff's office specifically credited the teachers and the students for doing the right thing by ignoring those requests and staying locked.

verification.notes: The October 10 JCSO update confirms that some officers identified themselves and asked locked-down classrooms to open, that teachers and students correctly kept doors locked, and that multiple agencies assisted. It does not expressly say only mutual-aid officers made the requests or separately declare county deputies compliant, so the citation overstates the source.

records.text: Candace Owens said the sheriff's revised timeline placed the substitute deputy en route from Conifer High School to a car crash when the Evergreen shooting call arrived, but no crash location, report number, parties, or independent corroboration had been released.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And they said, no, actually what happened was the sheriff's office revised this. The deputy had actually started his morning at Conifer. ... Then he made the drive to Evergreen. He stayed at Evergreen for about an hour. Then he drove back to Conifer. ... Then he was dispatched from Conifer High School to a car crash. And while en route to that car crash, that's when the call came in about the Evergreen shooting. ... Location of the crash he was originally dispatched to was never publicly released. Anything confirming that information has not been found by people who are around the clock working to confirm these details. ... no location, no other parties involved. It was reported but never independently corroborated.

verification.notes: The official revised account confirms that the substitute deputy left Evergreen for Conifer, was dispatched to a nearby car accident, and was redirected to the school before reaching the accident. The reviewed official release does not provide a crash location or report number, but absence of all independent corroboration cannot be conclusively established.
